For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

10	Truth convention: expected answers are what a careful analyst concludes after reading the initial file plus the optimal read path (at most three catalogue items); for INCOMPLETE and NOCONC cases, what the whole catalogue supports.

336	CASE OD2-HO-OBVWRONG-1 (OBVWRONG, technical): Buffering complaints in Kestria after a CDN provider switch
337	Setting: Orvanta Play is a fictional subscription video service operating in eleven markets. In October its smaller market, Kestria (about 400,000 subscribers), moved video delivery from its long-standing CDN provider, Corvane Edge, to a new provider, Tessaline Networks. Since then, buffering complaints in Kestria have risen sharply while every other market is stable. The regional VP blames the new CDN and wants to penalise the vendor and switch back.
338	Presenting request: From the CTO, 16 November: 'Before Thursday's leadership meeting I need a clear view of what is behind the Kestria buffering and whether we should approve Mireille's plan: SLA breach notice to Tessaline, October fees withheld, traffic moved back to Corvane. Tell me what is going on and what we should do next.'
339	INITIAL EVIDENCE
340	E1 [stage S1] Customer support ticketing system export (system-record): Ticketing system export, tag 'buffering/playback', market = Kestria. Weekly ticket counts: 22–28 Sep 118; 29 Sep–5 Oct 124; 6–12 Oct 433; 13–19 Oct 641; 20–26 Oct 628; 27 Oct–2 Nov 655; 3–9 Nov 637. Rate per 10,000 subscribers: 3.1 before 6 Oct, 16.0–16.4 from mid-October onward. All other markets combined: 2.8–3.2 per 10,000 every week, no trend. The device field on the ticket form is optional and is blank on 71% of Kestria tickets.
341	E2 [stage S1] Change management system, CHG-4471 (change-record): CHG-4471 — Kestria CDN provider migration. Scope: all Orvanta Play video delivery for Kestria (all apps, all ISPs) moved from Corvane Edge to Tessaline Networks, served from Tessaline's Varsk point of presence. Cutover: DNS weights shifted gradually from 8 Oct 22:00 to 9 Oct 04:10 local time; 100% of Kestria traffic on Tessaline from 04:10 on 9 Oct. Rollback: revert DNS weights, estimated 2 hours; Corvane contract for Kestria ends 31 Dec. All other markets remain on Corvane; no further migrations planned before 2027. Status: closed — successful, no errors during cutover.
342	E3 [stage S1] Playback quality dashboard (country view) (telemetry): Playback quality dashboard, country level. Daily rebuffering ratio (share of viewing time spent stalled), Kestria: 5 Oct 0.6%; 6 Oct 0.6%; 7 Oct 0.5%; 8 Oct 0.6%; 9 Oct 1.7%; 10 Oct 2.7%; 11 Oct 2.7%; 12–31 Oct 2.6–2.9%; 1–15 Nov 2.7–2.9%. Handball match nights (11, 18, 25 Oct): 2.7%, 2.8%, 2.7%. All other markets: 0.5–0.7% every day. Annotation, 11 Oct: 'Kestrian Handball League streaming launch; Kestria viewing hours +21% week on week.' The dashboard offers no breakdown below country level.
343	E4 [stage S1] Email from Mireille Okonta-Haas, VP Kestria, to the CTO and Head of Partnerships, 3 November (leadership-account): 'Since we moved Kestria to Tessaline on 8 October our buffering complaints have gone up fivefold, and nothing else in the region changed. Every other market is still on Corvane and is fine. October cancellations hit 3.4% of the base against 2.1% in September. Yes, the 1 October price rise was always going to cost us something, but this is the network. I want an SLA breach notice sent to Tessaline this week, their October fees withheld, and Kestria back on Corvane before that contract lapses. Also, please silence the Kestria rebuffering alert in the ops channel. We know the cause and it is paging people every night.'
344	E5 [stage S1] Product release digest, week 41, compiled by Product Operations (document): Release digest, week 41. 'Orvanta Play for smart TVs 5.2 is live in all markets as of 9 October (store listings approved 8 October). Highlights: redesigned home rails, 12% fewer crashes in beta, faster video start. Beta feedback positive. No playback regressions reported from any market. Mobile and web apps: no releases this sprint; next mobile release planned for December.'
345	E6 [stage S1] Call notes, Tobiah Lenn, senior network engineer, 14 October (staff-account): Notes from call with Tobiah Lenn. 'Tessaline's Varsk cache was cold after cutover. Their portal showed a hit ratio around 88% in the first week, against roughly 95% from Corvane. Our synthetic probes show p95 segment fetch time went from about 180 ms to about 215 ms. That is the kind of shift that tips players into stalls at peak time. I would put money on the CDN. The handball launch added load too, but the stalls started two days before that.'

Availability 99.995% (SLA 99.95%). Peak delivered throughput 412 Gbps against 900 Gbps provisioned capacity. Cache hit ratio, month average 92.6%, 'consistent with normal warm-up after onboarding'. Origin fetch error rate 0.002%; HTTP 5xx rate 0.004%. 'All SLA metrics were met for the period. We are aware of customer-reported rebuffering and are happy to support the investigation, but our edge metrics do not indicate a delivery fault.'
348	C2 [stage S1] Playback telemetry for Kestria, 12–25 October, broken down by client app, app version and ISP - Player session beacon warehouse, query by data engineering (telemetry): Session beacons, Kestria, 12–25 Oct. All sessions served by Tessaline (beacon CDN field). Rebuffering ratio by client (share of Kestria viewing hours in brackets): smart-TV app 5.2 — 5.9% (40%); smart-TV app 5.1, devices with auto-update off — 0.7% (8%); web player — 0.6% (22%); iOS/Android apps, unchanged since September — 0.7% (30%). By ISP, smart-TV 5.2: Kestnet 5.9%, Ostral Telecom 5.8%, Brevi Fibre 6.0%; all other clients on each of those ISPs 0.6–0.7%. Same breakdown for 24 Sep–7 Oct (Corvane): every client and every ISP 0.5–0.7%. Median video start time, 12–25 Oct: smart-TV 5.2 1.5 s; all other clients 2.4 s. Note: ad hoc warehouse query. Adding these breakdowns to the dashboard and alerts requires the pipeline rebuild scheduled for Q1 2027 (about six weeks).
349	C3 [stage S1] Release record and rollout configuration for smart-TV app 5.2 - Release management system, REL-TV-5.2 (change-record): REL-TV-5.2. Playback changes: adaptive-streaming startup buffer target lowered from 10 s to 4 s; switching up in quality allowed once 2 s is buffered (previously 6 s). Rationale: 'supports video start-time OKR'. Both values sit in server-side remote-config profile abr_v2 and can be reverted per market without a new app build; changes take effect within about an hour. Rollout gate: Kestria 100% from 9 Oct 06:00 (selected as canary market; TVs auto-update within ~48 h); all other markets 0%; next stage: all markets on 20 Nov. Store listings approved in all markets 8 Oct. Pre-release dogfood: 380 employee TVs in Dravia, served by Corvane, 24 Sep–8 Oct: rebuffering 5.7% on 5.2 versus 0.6% on 5.1. Ticket QA-2291: 'deferred until after general availability'.

353	C7 [stage S1] Kestria viewing hours and concurrency by day, 1 October–15 November - Content analytics (telemetry): Kestria viewing hours per day: 1–10 Oct average 1.92 million; 11 Oct–15 Nov average 2.31 million (+20%). Handball League share of viewing on match nights: 38%. Peak concurrent streams: 214,000 before 11 Oct; 268,000 on match nights afterwards. Share of viewing by device class unchanged across the period: smart TV 48%, mobile 30%, web 22%.
354	C8 [stage S1] CDN cutover execution log, CHG-4471, 8–9 October - Network operations runbook log (log): 8 Oct 22:00 DNS weight Tessaline 10%. 23:15 25%. 9 Oct 00:30 50%. 02:15 origin-shield HTTP 503 burst lasting 41 s, auto-recovered, 0.3% of requests in that minute affected. 03:20 75%. 04:10 100%. Health checks green throughout apart from 02:15. Post-cutover validation 04:30: test streams started successfully from Kestnet, Ostral and Brevi Fibre test lines. Change closed 05:05 by on-call network engineer.

rulings.explanation: The task defines 'association-only' as the two conditions co-occurring or correlating in the evidence without causation being established. It reserves 'unknown' for evidence that is 'insufficient even to show association'. The evidence does show co-occurrence. Kestria rebuffering rose from 9 Oct and stayed at 2.6–2.9% for the rest of October (E3). Kestria cancellations rose to 3.4% in October from 2.1% in September (E4, C6). The objection is that a confounder (the 1 Oct price rise) means association isn't shown. That mixes up association with causal identification. A confounder is exactly why the right label is association-only rather than causal. It does not erase the observed co-occurrence. No evidence counts against the link, so 'contradicted' does not apply. The exit survey has no quality option (C6) and does not separate the two causes, so 'causal' is also out. Read with the stated semantics, association-only is the single defensible answer.
rulings.fix: No change required. Optional hardening: state in E4 or C6 that the cancellation rise was concentrated after 9 Oct, or give weekly cancellation counts. That would make the temporal co-occurrence explicit beyond a single monthly figure.
